INTRODUCTIONM
You may be asking why aircraft need three phase, 400 Hz AC power supplies? Most electronic equipment operates on DC.
The alternating current produced by the aircraft generator is converted to DC by the three phase 400 Hz power supply system.
To operate DC electronic equipment, the AC power must be changed to DC before it can be used.
Due to size and weight limitations on aircraft, using three phase 400 Hz power allows for small and efficient equipment design as you will see.
Consequently, to convert three phase 400 Hz AC power to DC takes a three phase 400 Hz power supply.
Let's begin the lesson on THREE PHASE POWER GENERATION....................
LESSON MENU
A three phase 400 Hz power supply is no different than any other AC power supply.
DISCUSSION
An AC input is applied to the rectifier circuit first.
The rectifier changes AC to pulsating DC.
The rectifier circuit uses standard diodes in halfwave, fullwave and bridge rectifier configurations to change the AC to a pulsating DC.
DEFINITION
HALF WAVE RECTIFIER - The diode only conducts when forward biased. Thus only the positive alternation (half wave) of the sine wave reaches the load. AC is changed to Pulsating DC.

FULL WAVE RECTIFIER - The diode only conducts when forward biased but, each alternation (full wave) of the sine wave reaches the load due to the center tapped transformer and the two diodes. This changes AC to Pulsating DC.
DEFINITION

BRIDGE RECTIFIER - The diodes only conduct when forward biased but, each alternation (full wave) of the sine wave reaches the load due to the use of the four diodes (no center tapped transformer). This changes AC to Pulsating DC.
DEFINITION
Once the AC is changed to pulsating DC, it is filtered to produce pure DC.
Filters consist of a capacitor, a resistor and capacitor or an inductor and capacitor.
DEFINITION

CAPACITOR FILTER - The capacitor will charge up to the average voltage level of the applied pulsating DC. The charging and discharging of the capacitor when the pulsating DC is applied produces a smooth or filtered output.
RESISTOR CAPACITOR FILTER - The two capacitors will charge up to the average voltage level of the applied pulsating DC.
DEFINITION
INDUCTOR CAPACITOR FILTER - The two capacitors will charge up to the average voltage level of the applied pulsating DC.
DEFINITION
Finally, the pure DC is applied to a voltage regulator that maintains a constant voltage output even if the load on the power supply changes.
Normally, a zener diode or transistor voltage regulator is used.....
DEFINITION

ZENER REGULATOR - The zener diode will produce a constant output voltage as long as the input voltage is above the zener diodes breakdown voltage. This is why changes in the output load have no effect on the output voltage, the zener changes its internal resistance.
DEFINITION
TRANSISTOR REGULATOR - The conduction of the transistor is changed to compensate for output voltage variation by comparing the output voltage with a reference voltage (set by the zener diode).

Now, let's look at three phase 400 Hz power and find out why it is used instead of 1 phase 60 Hz power.
If you viewed one phase power with an oscilloscope, you would see one varying voltage level in the shape of a sine wave.
If it was changed to DC, you would get an average value of DC power out.
Three phase power has three varying voltage levels of equal amplitude and frequency but, at different phases.
Phase 1 or 1, varies from +V to -V just like one phase power. It is used as the reference phase.
Phase 2 or 2, also varies from +V to -V but starts 120 degrees from 1.
Phase 3 or 3, also varies from +V to -V but starts 240 degrees from 1 or 120 degrees from 2 (all phases are 120 degrees apart).
Changing three phase power to DC produces a higher DC voltage than 1 phase power.
Comparing one phase power to three phase power, you can see that the three phase contains MORE POWER.
This is very important when the size and weight of the power generating equipment is limited - such as in aircraft.
Most AC motors and other AC mechanical devices operate more efficiently on three phase power. Equipment size and weight is also reduced.
The next question we will look at is why use 400 Hz? Most equipment used in factories and your home is 50 or 60 Hz.
Again, it has to do with changing AC to DC and the efficiency of AC motors and other AC mechanical devices.
As you can see, the average power delivered by 400 Hz is greater than 60 Hz due to the higher frequency.
Since the average power is higher, converting the power to DC produces a higher DC voltage. Motors and other AC devices operate more efficiently using higher frequencies.
Again, since space and weight are limited on aircraft, 400 Hz power is used to reduce the size and weight of equipment.
It is not uncommon to find a low voltage 10 kHz power system on an aircraft.
Which term can be used to describe a piece of equipment that uses three phase 400 Hz power?
Three phase 400 Hz equipment can be smaller, have less weight and receive more power from a source than one phase 60 Hz equipment. They are not less efficient.....

Finally, let's look at a typical three phase 400 Hz power supply. This is the power supply used in the experiment.
The power supply consists of these standard three circuits:
The rectifier converts three phase 400 Hz power to a pulsating DC.
A typical rectifier contains three transformers and six diodes.
The three transformers, one for each phase, provide isolation and will step up or step down the voltage depending on the output requirements.
There are six diodes used to form a bridge circuit for each one of the three phases. This is the main difference between one phase and three phase power supplies.
Diodes D1, D2, D3 and D4 form a bridge rectifier for phase 1 and produce a full wave pulsating DC output.

BRIDGE RECTIFIER - Bottom of transformer NEGATIVE - current flow via bottom of transformer, D4, ground, up through load, D1, to top of transformer. Bottom of transformer POSITIVE - current flow via top of transformer, D2, ground, up through load, D3, to bottom of transformer. Current flow through load in same direction for both alternation.
Diodes D3, D4, D5 and D6 form a bridge rectifier for phase 2 and produce a full wave pulsating DC output displaced 120 degrees from phase 1.

BRIDGE RECTIFIER - Bottom of transformer NEGATIVE - current flow via bottom of transformer, D6, ground, up through load, D3, to top of transformer. Bottom of transformer POSITIVE - current flow via top of transformer, D4, ground, up through load, D5, to bottom of transformer. Current flow through load in same direction for both alternation.
Diodes D1, D2, D5 and D6 form a bridge rectifier for phase 3 and produce a full wave pulsating DC output 240 degrees displaced from phase 1 and 120 degrees displaced from phase 2.

BRIDGE RECTIFIER - Bottom of transformer NEGATIVE - current flow via bottom of transformer, D6, ground, up through load, D5, to top of transformer. Bottom of transformer POSITIVE - current flow via top of transformer, D6, ground, up through load, D5, to bottom of transformer. Current flow through load in same direction for both alternation.
The result is a pulsating DC output, or DC with a ripple. Ripple is commonly used to describe the DC variations when AC is rectified.

After the filtering, the pure DC is regulated to maintain a constant output.
The regulator circuit used in the experiment consists of a voltage regulator and an overcurrent protection circuit.
Voltage regulation is accomplished by Q2, D7, and U1.
Conduction of the voltage regulator Q2 varies to compensate for output voltage variations.
The conduction of Q2 is controlled by the voltage applied to its base from the operational amplifier in the differential configuration.
The conduction of Q2 is controlled by the voltage applied to its base from the operational amplifier in the differential configuration.
DEFINITION
DIFFERENTIAL AMPLIFIER - The operational amplifier produces a DC output in proportion to the difference between the + or non-inverting input and the - or inverting input.
The negative input is a sample of the output voltage through the voltage divider action of R8 and R1.
The positive input is a constant voltage developed by zener diode D7 as adjusted by R3 (C2 acts as another filter blocking DC and R2 supplies the voltage to D7).
The difference between the + and - inputs of U1 produce a positive voltage to the base of Q2 which causes it to conduct at a certain rate, producing a voltage level to the load.
If the load changes causing the output voltage to decrease, the voltage applied to the negative input of U1 decreases.
With a constant voltage applied to the positive input of U1 and the negative input voltage being less, the positive output of U1 increases.
The increased positive output voltage of U1 is applied to the base of Q2 and the conduction of Q2 increases.
With Q2 conducting more, the output voltage increases to the original set level.
If the load changes causing the output voltage to increase, the voltage applied to the negative input of U1 increases.
With a constant voltage applied to the positive input of U1 and a higher negative input voltage, the positive output of U1 decreases.
The decreased positive output voltage of U1 is applied to the base of Q2 and the conduction of Q2 decreases.
With Q2 conducting less, the output voltage decreases to the original level as set.
U1 controls the conduction of Q2 to maintain a constant output voltage even if the load changes. This is voltage regulation.
The overcurrent protection circuit is made up of Q1 and R4, R5 and R9 as illustrated.
R4, R5 and R9 are small value resistors that develop a small voltage drop which has very little effect on the output voltage.
With the base and emitter of Q1 connected across R4, R5 and R9, Q1 is not biased ON. This is due to the small voltage drop of the resistors.
With Q1 OFF, there is no effect in the circuit and output current continues to flow.
However, if the output current increases to a high enough level, as set by R5, the voltage drop of R4, R5 and R9 will be sufficient to bias Q1 ON.
When Q1 turns ON, the base and emitter of Q2 are shorted which turns Q2 OFF and the output current stops flowing.
When the current flow stops, Q1 will turn OFF allowing Q2 to turn ON, producing current.
If the current is still excessive, Q1 turns ON turning Q2 OFF again. The process will continue until the current is no longer excessive.
The net effect is that when current is excessive, Q2 turns ON and OFF which effectively lowers the output voltage so current is kept within the set limits.

In this experiment, you will study the operation of and troubleshoot a three phase 400 Hz power supply.
EXPERIMENT
The three phase 400 Hz power supply, PC130-230, is supported by two other cards that will be located in PC1 and PC3 positions.
It is used to verify correct operation of the voltage regulator on PC130-230. This is accomplished by applying different loads using the PC130-290 card.
The switches along the top portion of the card are used to apply different fixed loads and R1 is used to vary the load.
The PC130-229 card is an electronic Three Phase Generator..
It is used in place of a mechanical three phase alternator or generator to produce the three phase 400 Hz power.
You will adjust the potentiometers on the card to produce a clean three phase 400 Hz output.
Basically, U1 produces a sine wave output that is split to drive three power amplifiers that have 120 degree phase differences.
The three devices on top of the card are connected to a heat sink. U4, U5 and U6 are power amplifiers and will become hot and will burn you if touched.
Finally, PC130-230 is the Power Supply.....................
It is the circuit that you studied in the theory portion of the lesson with the addition of test points and test console connector pins.

You should have seen the voltage decrease. What's happening is that the load causes excessive current and Q1 is turned ON.
This action turns Q2 off stopping the current flow. As the current flow now decreases, Q1 turns off and Q2 turns back on. The process goes on and on.
In other words, the output voltage is decreased to keep the output current at a safe level by turning Q2 on and off.
